source.title: Christian Apologetics
allOriginalHeadings: What are the general categories of Christian apologetics?
Imagine someone says, “The sparse evidence for your God requires that I assign a very low credence to your God’s existence.” How might each category of apologist respond?
For each apologetic category, provide a hypothetical dialogue between an apologist and a philosopher, with the philosopher revealing the weaknesses in the apologetics approach.

How might any of these apologetic approaches deal with the absurdity of an omnipresent and omnipotent God wanting a relationship with humans, but requiring that those humans read a holy book to come to know him?
Provide 20 discussion questions relevant to the content above.
source.modelAttribution: ChatGPT logos in original source; displayed as editorial editions

responseDecisions.1.1: Restored all twelve approaches and original overview/method/proponent lists. Clarified overlapping categories, proper basicality, qualified historical associations, Kant practical faith, and compatibility versus positive evidence. Effective descriptions retained.
responseDecisions.2.1: Restored all twelve table rows; rewrote replies as explicitly hypothetical, differentiated changes to evidence from changes to justification standard, and stated narrow claims without treating apologetic assertions as findings.
responseDecisions.3.1: Restored all twelve dialogues with 96 turns in source order. Repaired physics/quantum, historical independence and mass-hallucination assertions, description/normativity conflations, basic belief, Bayesian dependence, modal reversal, and cultural/biological overclaims. Preserved critical progression and final skeptical turns.
responseDecisions.4.1: Restored twelve response/strength/weakness comparisons. Addressed exact curator objection, rejected universal personal-reading premise without evading relational hiddenness, distinguished stated theological proposals from demonstrated access, and challenged free-will/mystery as unsupported answers.
responseDecisions.5.1: Restored fifteen question/expandable-answer pairs, repaired dependent-evidence, modal argument, basicality and hiddenness keys. Three effective source answers retained.
responseDecisions.6.1: All twenty source questions in order; sixteen verbatim. Four revised to reflect corrected cumulative, modal, evidence and hiddenness distinctions.

manualChecks.scope: Hypothetical dialogues, not quotations or definitive surveys of Christian traditions; critical conclusions concern support for claims.

research.checked: Primary preface account of extended Aquinas/Calvin model: proper function, truth-directed process and conditional scope. Web deep-open failed; direct PDF download and local text extraction succeeded. No whole-book reading claimed.
Pages 10–11 of PDF: author explicitly excludes empty tomb from strict minimal facts, distinguishes early proclamation and related premises. No independent survey of scholarly consensus claimed.
Proponent’s discussion of necessary existence and possibility; corrected asymmetric dismissal of rival possibility. Critical assessment is editorial reasoning, not attributed to Craig.
Official account distinguishes Christian Word from merely written text; used as one denominational counterexample to universal personal-reading requirement, not as evidence the religion is true.

Liu/Ochman 2007 abstract and indexed PMC search extract: comparative sequence evidence for stepwise flagellar development. University PDF link was 404 and replaced with PubMed. Direct PMC access challenged; not bypassed. No complete evolutionary reconstruction or replication claim; PubMed lists an erratum not assessed here.
